newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says Netherlands example to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says Netherlands example to Europe.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Monday that the Netherlands was now more or less a model country on the European continent.

In a speech congratulating Dutch central banker Wim Duisenberg on gaining a 'European Bank of the Year" award, Tietmeyer praised Duisenberg for his policies, adding Dutch politicians had also taken reform steps at the right time.
"To a certain extent, The Netherlands today is the model country, the example for the continent," he said.

"While others moaned about the flood of economic challenges, the Dutch started earlier to make themselves fit," he said, adding that they had overhauled their welfare systems and made the labour market more flexible."
"To be sure, the Netherlands still has some problems today. But the corrections are paying off," he said.

Looking ahead to European monetary union, Tietmeyer noted that Duisenberg was taking over as head of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner to the European Central Bank, in the middle of the year.

Acknowledging that Duisenberg's credentials made him well-suited to this job, Tietmeyer added, "He is probably also the natural candidate for the position of future president of the European Central Bank."
